findings.body: The HTTP request context is canceled when the handler finishes, immediately canceling the derived context and causing create, update, delete, or delete-collection writes to legacy storage to fail nondeterministically.
findings.evidence: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, errors.New("legacy create timeout"))
findings.failure_mode: The primary unified-store write succeeds and is returned to the client, but its legacy mirror is canceled and never persisted.
findings.impact: The HTTP request context is canceled when the handler finishes, immediately canceling the derived context and causing create, update, delete, or delete-collection writes to legacy storage to fail nondeterministically.
findings.root_cause: All four background legacy operations derive their timeout context directly from the request-scoped parent context.
findings.suggested_fix: Detach each background operation from request cancellation with context.WithoutCancel(ctx), then apply the ten-second timeout to that detached context while preserving required values such as logging metadata.
findings.title: Asynchronous legacy writes inherit a request context that is canceled when the response completes
findings.trigger: A Mode3 write returns from the API handler before its newly launched legacy goroutine completes, which is the normal asynchronous execution path.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 51 shows ctx derived from request context with WithTimeoutCause. When HTTP handler returns, parent ctx cancels, immediately canceling the derived context before the 10-second timeout. This affects all four async legacy operations (Create, Update, Delete, DeleteCollection) which all use the same pattern.

findings.body: The Prometheus histogram's `kind` label receives a unique value per object, creating unbounded time-series cardinality and making Mode3 delete metrics inconsistent with error and other-operation metrics.
findings.failure_mode: Monitoring allocates a new histogram series for each deleted object name.
findings.impact: The Prometheus histogram's `kind` label receives a unique value per object, creating unbounded time-series cardinality and making Mode3 delete metrics inconsistent with error and other-operation metrics.
findings.root_cause: The success metric call supplies the resource name in the positional argument reserved for kind.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass options.Kind instead of name to recordStorageDuration.
findings.title: Delete metrics use object names as the kind label
findings.trigger: Successful deletes are performed for many distinct object names.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 106 shows d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) where 'name' is the object name, not options.Kind. Compare to line 103 which correctly uses options.Kind. This creates unbounded metric cardinality as each unique object name becomes a label value.

pr.body:
**What is this feature?**

Mode 3 will work the following way:

reads (get, list) : only use unified storage
writes (create, update, delete, delete-collection) : write to unified storage and then asynchronously, write to legacy, just as a safe measure.

raw_findings.body: SetDualWritingMode only implements Mode1/Mode2 transitions, so the server continues running Mode1 or Mode2; Mode3 reads and asynchronous legacy writes are not exercised or enabled through normal configuration.

raw_findings.root_cause: The existing synchronous dual-write test routine is reused unchanged for a mode whose secondary writes now complete asynchronously.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Make the Mode3 cases use eventual assertions for legacy visibility and deletion, or add an explicit synchronization hook for tests; apply the same treatment to both file and unified-storage Mode3 cases.
raw_findings.title: Mode 3 integration tests assume synchronous legacy consistency
raw_findings.trigger: The test actually runs Mode3 and the legacy goroutine has not completed when doPlaylistTests immediately reads the legacy API after a Kubernetes create or update.

raw_findings.body: Legacy storage can be destroyed concurrently with a write, causing errors or races, and graceful shutdown can lose accepted mirror writes.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Shutdown closes backend resources before accepted asynchronous operations finish.
raw_findings.impact: Legacy storage can be destroyed concurrently with a write, causing errors or races, and graceful shutdown can lose accepted mirror writes.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch launches unmanaged goroutines while DualWriterMode3.Destroy has no coordination with them.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Track background work with a lifecycle-owned wait group or worker queue, stop accepting work during shutdown, and drain or cancel it before destroying either backend.
raw_findings.title: Background legacy writes are not drained before storage destruction
raw_findings.trigger: The server shuts down or calls Destroy while any asynchronous legacy create, update, delete, or delete-collection operation remains in flight.

raw_findings.body: Outstanding goroutines, request objects, and backend calls grow with write rate, potentially exhausting memory, connections, or legacy capacity and destabilizing the server.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A slow legacy backend turns sustained write traffic into an unbounded number of concurrent background operations.
raw_findings.impact: Outstanding goroutines, request objects, and backend calls grow with write rate, potentially exhausting memory, connections, or legacy capacity and destabilizing the server.
raw_findings.root_cause: Asynchronous replication has no concurrency limit or backpressure mechanism.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Route secondary writes through a bounded worker pool or queue with explicit overload behavior and shutdown handling instead of spawning an unrestricted goroutine per request.
raw_findings.title: One goroutine per write allows an unbounded legacy backlog
raw_findings.trigger: Mode3 receives writes faster than legacy storage can process them, especially while legacy calls approach the ten-second timeout.

finding.impact: The new tests only validate the synchronous unified-store result and still pass when the defining Mode3 secondary-write behavior is broken.
finding.root_cause: The test returns to result assertions immediately after the primary operation and never verifies completion of the spawned goroutine.

validated_findings.body: SetDualWritingMode only implements Mode1/Mode2 transitions, so the server continues running Mode1 or Mode2; Mode3 reads and asynchronous legacy writes are not exercised or enabled through normal configuration.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The desired configuration is silently ignored and tests labeled Mode3 execute a different dual-writer implementation.
validated_findings.impact: SetDualWritingMode only implements Mode1/Mode2 transitions, so the server continues running Mode1 or Mode2; Mode3 reads and asynchronous legacy writes are not exercised or enabled through normal configuration.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch adds Mode3 configuration and tests without extending the persisted-mode transition state machine beyond Mode1 and Mode2.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Implement the permitted transition into Mode3 in SetDualWritingMode, normally from Mode2 after its synchronization gate, and make the integration test assert the effective mode before running CRUD checks.
validated_findings.title: Mode 3 configuration never transitions the persisted dual-writer mode
validated_findings.trigger: An instance with an unset, Mode1, or Mode2 persisted mode is configured with desired Mode3, as these new integration cases do.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that SetDualWritingMode only implements Mode1/Mode2 transitions is based on dualwriter.go lines 198-218, but the patch only adds test configuration for Mode3. NewDualWriter at line 117 already handles Mode3 by calling newDualWriterMode3. The test configuration passes Mode3 to DualWriterDesiredModes which flows through to NewDualWriter, not SetDualWritingMode for runtime transitions.

validated_findings.body: The HTTP request context is canceled when the handler finishes, immediately canceling the derived context and causing create, update, delete, or delete-collection writes to legacy storage to fail nondeterministically.
validated_findings.evidence: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, errors.New("legacy create timeout"))
validated_findings.failure_mode: The primary unified-store write succeeds and is returned to the client, but its legacy mirror is canceled and never persisted.
validated_findings.impact: The HTTP request context is canceled when the handler finishes, immediately canceling the derived context and causing create, update, delete, or delete-collection writes to legacy storage to fail nondeterministically.
validated_findings.root_cause: All four background legacy operations derive their timeout context directly from the request-scoped parent context.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Detach each background operation from request cancellation with context.WithoutCancel(ctx), then apply the ten-second timeout to that detached context while preserving required values such as logging metadata.
validated_findings.title: Asynchronous legacy writes inherit a request context that is canceled when the response completes
validated_findings.trigger: A Mode3 write returns from the API handler before its newly launched legacy goroutine completes, which is the normal asynchronous execution path.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 51 shows ctx derived from request context with WithTimeoutCause. When HTTP handler returns, parent ctx cancels, immediately canceling the derived context before the 10-second timeout. This affects all four async legacy operations (Create, Update, Delete, DeleteCollection) which all use the same pattern.

validated_findings.body: The callback is invoked once by unified storage and again by legacy storage against different old objects, so legacy may persist different data, reject the unified resource version, or apply a non-repeatable transformation twice.
validated_findings.evidence: _, _, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, createValidation, updateValidation, forceAllowCreate, options)
validated_findings.failure_mode: One logical update produces divergent objects or a failed legacy mirror despite the authoritative update succeeding.
validated_findings.impact: The callback is invoked once by unified storage and again by legacy storage against different old objects, so legacy may persist different data, reject the unified resource version, or apply a non-repeatable transformation twice.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch removed the fixed-result updateWrapper and reuses the original UpdatedObjectInfo for the second backend.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Capture and deep-copy the object returned by the successful unified update and pass legacy storage an updateWrapper whose UpdatedObject returns that exact result, as the previous implementation did.
validated_findings.title: Legacy updates recompute the request against the wrong old object
validated_findings.trigger: A PATCH, apply, transform, or other UpdatedObjectInfo computes its result from the supplied old object, and the unified and legacy stores have different metadata or content.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 139 shows d.Legacy.Update called with original objInfo instead of a fixed-result wrapper. The old code (removed lines 101-107) used updateWrapper with captured updated object. Now UpdatedObjectInfo.UpdatedObject will be called against legacy's old object, potentially producing different results than unified storage.

validated_findings.body: The new Mode3 integration cases become scheduler-dependent and can fail intermittently even when the documented asynchronous behavior is correct.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Tests read legacy storage before the mirror operation completes and report transient stale data as a failure.
validated_findings.impact: The new Mode3 integration cases become scheduler-dependent and can fail intermittently even when the documented asynchronous behavior is correct.
validated_findings.root_cause: The existing synchronous dual-write test routine is reused unchanged for a mode whose secondary writes now complete asynchronously.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Make the Mode3 cases use eventual assertions for legacy visibility and deletion, or add an explicit synchronization hook for tests; apply the same treatment to both file and unified-storage Mode3 cases.
validated_findings.title: Mode 3 integration tests assume synchronous legacy consistency
validated_findings.trigger: The test actually runs Mode3 and the legacy goroutine has not completed when doPlaylistTests immediately reads the legacy API after a Kubernetes create or update.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: While the test does reuse doPlaylistTests for Mode3, the claim assumes tests will fail due to async behavior. However, the tests primarily verify k8s API responses which come from unified storage (the synchronous path). Legacy consistency is not directly asserted in doPlaylistTests based on the provided context.

validated_findings.body: Legacy storage can be destroyed concurrently with a write, causing errors or races, and graceful shutdown can lose accepted mirror writes.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Shutdown closes backend resources before accepted asynchronous operations finish.
validated_findings.impact: Legacy storage can be destroyed concurrently with a write, causing errors or races, and graceful shutdown can lose accepted mirror writes.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch launches unmanaged goroutines while DualWriterMode3.Destroy has no coordination with them.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Track background work with a lifecycle-owned wait group or worker queue, stop accepting work during shutdown, and drain or cancel it before destroying either backend.
validated_findings.title: Background legacy writes are not drained before storage destruction
validated_findings.trigger: The server shuts down or calls Destroy while any asynchronous legacy create, update, delete, or delete-collection operation remains in flight.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This describes the same root cause as candidate 1 - unmanaged goroutines with request-derived contexts. The shutdown/Destroy concern is a consequence of the same pattern. Both would be fixed by proper lifecycle management.

validated_findings.body: Outstanding goroutines, request objects, and backend calls grow with write rate, potentially exhausting memory, connections, or legacy capacity and destabilizing the server.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A slow legacy backend turns sustained write traffic into an unbounded number of concurrent background operations.
validated_findings.impact: Outstanding goroutines, request objects, and backend calls grow with write rate, potentially exhausting memory, connections, or legacy capacity and destabilizing the server.
validated_findings.root_cause: Asynchronous replication has no concurrency limit or backpressure mechanism.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Route secondary writes through a bounded worker pool or queue with explicit overload behavior and shutdown handling instead of spawning an unrestricted goroutine per request.
validated_findings.title: One goroutine per write allows an unbounded legacy backlog
validated_findings.trigger: Mode3 receives writes faster than legacy storage can process them, especially while legacy calls approach the ten-second timeout.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: While unbounded goroutines are a valid concern, this is a design/performance consideration rather than a concrete bug. The 10-second timeout provides some bound. Without evidence of actual resource exhaustion or specific thresholds, this is speculative.

validated_findings.body: Delete returns NotFound without deleting the legacy copy, leaving the two stores divergent and allowing stale data to reappear if legacy storage is later used for rollback or recovery.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A stale legacy record survives a delete request indefinitely.
validated_findings.impact: Delete returns NotFound without deleting the legacy copy, leaving the two stores divergent and allowing stale data to reappear if legacy storage is later used for rollback or recovery.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new early return treats NotFound like every other storage error and removes the previous legacy-cleanup path.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Special-case apierrors.IsNotFound from unified storage and still schedule the legacy deletion, while preserving the authoritative response semantics for the caller.
validated_findings.title: A unified-store NotFound no longer removes a stale legacy object
validated_findings.trigger: The requested object is already absent from unified storage but remains in legacy storage because of an earlier partial write, migration, or replication failure.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 104 shows early return on error, but the claim about NotFound not cleaning legacy is incorrect. The old code (removed lines 65-69) only logged NotFound errors from legacy, it didn't have special cleanup logic. The new code returns the unified storage error directly, which is consistent behavior.

validated_findings.body: The Prometheus histogram's `kind` label receives a unique value per object, creating unbounded time-series cardinality and making Mode3 delete metrics inconsistent with error and other-operation metrics.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Monitoring allocates a new histogram series for each deleted object name.
validated_findings.impact: The Prometheus histogram's `kind` label receives a unique value per object, creating unbounded time-series cardinality and making Mode3 delete metrics inconsistent with error and other-operation metrics.
validated_findings.root_cause: The success metric call supplies the resource name in the positional argument reserved for kind.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass options.Kind instead of name to recordStorageDuration.
validated_findings.title: Delete metrics use object names as the kind label
validated_findings.trigger: Successful deletes are performed for many distinct object names.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 106 shows d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) where 'name' is the object name, not options.Kind. Compare to line 103 which correctly uses options.Kind. This creates unbounded metric cardinality as each unique object name becomes a label value.

validated_findings.body: The failed unified call is absent from storage error metrics and is falsely reported as a failed legacy operation, corrupting latency and error-rate telemetry.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Operational dashboards attribute a unified-store create failure to the wrong backend.
validated_findings.impact: The failed unified call is absent from storage error metrics and is falsely reported as a failed legacy operation, corrupting latency and error-rate telemetry.
validated_findings.root_cause: The storage error branch invokes the legacy metric recorder.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Call recordStorageDuration for this primary-storage failure.
validated_findings.title: Create failures are recorded in the legacy histogram
validated_findings.trigger: Unified storage returns an error from a Mode3 create.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 45 shows d.recordLegacyDuration called when Storage.Create fails. This records a storage failure as a legacy duration metric. The correct call should be recordStorageDuration as done on line 48 for success. This misattributes the error to the wrong backend.

validated_findings.body: The failed unified update is missing from storage error metrics and appears as a legacy failure even though legacy was never called.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Metrics identify the wrong failing backend and report a legacy operation that did not occur.
validated_findings.impact: The failed unified update is missing from storage error metrics and appears as a legacy failure even though legacy was never called.
validated_findings.root_cause: The unified update error path selects the legacy duration metric.
validated_findings.title: Update failures are recorded in the legacy histogram
validated_findings.trigger: Unified storage returns an error from a Mode3 update.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 129 shows d.recordLegacyDuration called when Storage.Update fails, but legacy was never called. Should be recordStorageDuration. Same pattern as candidate 8.

validated_findings.body: Storage metrics receive a second DeleteCollection observation while the legacy histogram receives none, distorting both backend latency and error rates.
validated_findings.evidence: d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)
validated_findings.failure_mode: Telemetry counts a legacy operation under the wrong backend.
validated_findings.impact: Storage metrics receive a second DeleteCollection observation while the legacy histogram receives none, distorting both backend latency and error rates.
validated_findings.root_cause: The legacy DeleteCollection completion invokes the storage metric recorder.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use recordLegacyDuration for the asynchronous legacy call.
validated_findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection duration is recorded as a storage operation
validated_findings.trigger: The asynchronous legacy DeleteCollection call finishes in Mode3.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 166 shows d.recordStorageDuration called for the legacy DeleteCollection result. Should be recordLegacyDuration. This is the inverse error - legacy operation recorded as storage.

validated_findings.body: Downstream logs omit the delete operation's name, kind, and method fields even though an enriched `log` value was constructed immediately before this line.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Delete-related backend logs cannot be reliably correlated with the affected resource and operation.
validated_findings.impact: Downstream logs omit the delete operation's name, kind, and method fields even though an enriched `log` value was constructed immediately before this line.
validated_findings.root_cause: The context is populated with the base logger instead of the operation-scoped logger.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass log rather than d.Log to klog.NewContext.
validated_findings.title: Delete passes the unscoped logger to downstream storage
validated_findings.trigger: Unified or legacy delete code obtains its logger from the supplied context.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 97 shows ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) but line 96 creates enriched 'log' with name, kind, method. The enriched logger is discarded and base logger is used for context, losing operation-specific fields in downstream logs.
